capital-npl.summary: A landlocked country on the southern slopes of the Himalayas, home to Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha. The capital is Kathmandu.
facts: Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, sits on its border with China.
It is the only country whose flag is not a rectangle.

capital-twn.summary: An island between the East China Sea and the South China Sea where bubble tea was invented. Its main city is Taipei.
facts: Taipei 101 was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010.
On the Lantern Festival, people in Pingxi release sky lanterns inscribed with their wishes.

capital-tls.summary: A mostly Catholic nation that occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor. The capital is Dili.
facts: After rule by Portugal and then Indonesia, it became independent in 2002.
Tetum and Portuguese are both official languages.

capital-lao.summary: Southeast Asia's only landlocked country, where sticky rice is the staple food. The capital is Vientiane.
facts: The old town of Luang Prabang is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Mekong flows north to south along its western border.

capital-lbn.summary: A country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean where power is shared among several Christian and Muslim sects. The capital is Beirut.
facts: A Lebanon cedar sits in the center of its flag.
It is the land where the ancient Phoenicians built their port cities.

capital-mys.summary: A country on the Malay Peninsula and Borneo whose favorite dish is nasi lemak, rice cooked in coconut milk. The capital is Kuala Lumpur.
facts: Government functions have moved to Putrajaya, but Kuala Lumpur remains the capital by law.
The Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.

capital-mdv.summary: An Indian Ocean nation of coral islands, where honeymooners flock to overwater bungalow resorts. The capital is Malé.
facts: It is made up of more than 1,000 coral islands.
With an average elevation of about 1.5 meters (5 feet), it is the lowest-lying country in the world.

capital-mng.summary: A landlocked country of grassy steppes where many nomads still herd livestock and live in portable felt tents called gers. The capital is Ulaanbaatar.
facts: Ulaanbaatar is the world's coldest capital, with an average annual temperature of around 0°C (32°F).
Karakorum, the capital of the Mongol Empire, stood in the Orkhon River valley to the west.

capital-mmr.summary: A Buddhist country on the western side of Indochina, where the golden Shwedagon Pagoda rises. The capital is Naypyidaw.
facts: In 2005 the capital moved from Yangon to Naypyidaw.
Thousands of Buddhist temples and stupas still stand on the plain of Bagan.

capital-bhr.summary: A small island nation in the Persian Gulf that hosts a Formula One race every year. The capital is Manama.
facts: A causeway links it to Saudi Arabia.
Its historic pearling trail is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

capital-bgd.summary: A country on the Ganges delta and a garment-export giant whose name often shows up on clothing labels. The capital is Dhaka.
facts: It split from Pakistan in 1971 after a nine-month war of independence.
International Mother Language Day on February 21 grew out of the 1952 protests in Dhaka to defend the Bengali language.

capital-vnm.summary: A long, narrow country in Indochina stretching north to south, home of pho noodle soup and banh mi sandwiches. The capital is Hanoi.
facts: The largest city is Ho Chi Minh City in the south, but the capital is Hanoi in the north.
The limestone islands of Ha Long Bay are a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site.

capital-btn.summary: A kingdom in the eastern Himalayas that limits tourist numbers by charging visitors a daily fee. The capital is Thimphu.
facts: In 1972 its fourth king put Gross National Happiness ahead of Gross National Product.
In Thimphu, police officers direct traffic with hand signals instead of traffic lights.

capital-prk.summary: A country on the northern half of the Korean Peninsula, ruled by three generations of one family since its regime was founded in 1948. The capital is Pyongyang.
facts: At the 2018 inter-Korean summit dinner, naengmyeon cold noodles from Pyongyang's Okryu-gwan restaurant were brought all the way to Panmunjom.
It joined the United Nations together with South Korea in September 1991.

capital-brn.summary: A kingdom on the north coast of Borneo whose oil and gas wealth means it levies no income tax. The capital is Bandar Seri Begawan.
facts: In the water village of Kampong Ayer, houses linked by wooden walkways line the river.
The Limbang district of Malaysia's Sarawak state splits the country into two pieces.

capital-sau.summary: A kingdom covering most of the Arabian Peninsula, chosen to host the 2034 World Cup. The capital is Riyadh.
facts: It is home to Mecca and Medina, the holy cities of Islam.
Oil first gushed out in 1938 at Dammam in the east.

capital-lka.summary: An island nation south of India, nicknamed the "Tear of the Indian Ocean" for its shape. The capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
facts: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital, while Colombo is the executive and judicial capital.
The "Ceylon" in Ceylon tea was the island nation's name until 1972.

capital-syr.summary: A country on the eastern Mediterranean whose capital gave its name to damask, a patterned silk. The capital is Damascus.
facts: Damascus is often counted among the oldest continuously inhabited cities.
In 2025 it officially adopted its current flag of green, white, and black stripes with three red stars.

capital-sgp.summary: A city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula, with rules so strict that chewing gum can't be sold freely. The city-state is its own capital.
facts: It became independent in 1965 after separating from the Federation of Malaysia.
Sitting on the Strait of Malacca, it runs one of the world's largest transshipment ports.

capital-are.summary: A federation of seven sheikhdoms that reclaimed land from the sea to build Palm Jumeirah, a palm-shaped artificial island. The capital is Abu Dhabi.
facts: Dubai is the largest city, but Abu Dhabi is the capital.
Dubai's Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world.

capital-arm.summary: A landlocked country in the South Caucasus that still uses its own alphabet, created in the early 5th century. The capital is Yerevan.
facts: In 301 it became the first country in the world to adopt Christianity as its state religion.
Mount Ararat, which its people regard as sacred, now lies in Turkey.

capital-aze.summary: A country on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, home to Yanar Dag, a hillside where underground gas keeps a fire burning nonstop. The capital is Baku.
facts: Lying 28 meters (92 feet) below sea level, Baku is the lowest capital in the world.
In 1901 the Baku oil fields produced more than half of the world's oil.

capital-afg.summary: A landlocked country between Central and South Asia, the setting of the novel “The Kite Runner.” The capital is Kabul.
facts: The Hindu Kush mountains divide the country into north and south.
In 2001 the Taliban destroyed the giant Buddhas of the Bamiyan Valley, a stop on the Silk Road.

capital-yem.summary: A country at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula; mocha coffee is named after its Red Sea port of Mocha. The capital is Sanaa.
facts: The tower houses of Sanaa's Old City, built of mud and fired brick, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Kingdom of Saba, said to be the land of the Queen of Sheba, grew rich on the frankincense trade.

capital-omn.summary: A country at the eastern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, where frankincense trees grow in the southern Dhofar region. The capital is Muscat.
facts: It faces Iran across the Strait of Hormuz.
In the 19th century it ruled as far as Zanzibar in East Africa.

capital-jor.summary: A country on the Dead Sea and the river it shares its name with, whose red desert of Wadi Rum served as a filming location for “The Martian.” The capital is Amman.
facts: It is home to Petra, an ancient city carved out of rock.
The Dead Sea's surface is the lowest point on land on Earth.

capital-uzb.summary: A landlocked Central Asian country home to many descendants of ethnic Koreans who were forcibly deported there. The capital is Tashkent.
facts: Samarkand and Bukhara were famous cities on the Silk Road.
It is one of the rare countries where you must cross two borders to reach the sea.

capital-irq.summary: The land between two rivers, where the base-60 system that splits an hour into 60 minutes was born. The capital is Baghdad.
facts: In Mesopotamia, between the two rivers, the Sumerians wrote in cuneiform.
Harun al-Rashid, the caliph of “One Thousand and One Nights,” ruled Abbasid Baghdad.

capital-irn.summary: The ancient land of Persia, a major producer of hand-woven carpets and saffron. The capital is Tehran.
facts: Persepolis is the site of the old capital of the Achaemenid dynasty.
The new year begins on the spring equinox, and the holiday is called Nowruz.

capital-isr.summary: A country on the eastern Mediterranean where buses mostly stop running on Saturday, the Sabbath. Its self-declared capital is Jerusalem.
facts: Jerusalem is a holy city for Judaism, Christianity, and Islam alike.
About nine in ten foreign embassies are in the Tel Aviv area rather than Jerusalem.

capital-ind.summary: A large South Asian country known for yoga, curry, and the Bollywood film industry. The capital is New Delhi.
facts: New Delhi is an administrative city planned and built under British rule.
The Taj Mahal, a Mughal mausoleum, is in Agra.

capital-idn.summary: A country made up of more than 17,000 islands. The capital is Jakarta.
facts: Jakarta remains the capital until a presidential decree is issued, and the move to Nusantara is underway.
Borobudur, on the island of Java, is the largest Buddhist monument in the world.

capital-jpn.summary: An island nation across the East Sea from Korea, known for anime and sushi. The capital is Tokyo.
facts: Tokyo grew after the shogunate set up there, back when the city was called Edo.
At 3,776 meters (12,388 feet), Mount Fuji is the country's highest mountain.

capital-geo.summary: A Caucasus country on the eastern shore of the Black Sea with a tradition of polyphonic choral singing. The capital is Tbilisi.
facts: Traces of winemaking from about 8,000 years ago have been found here.
A favorite dish is khachapuri, boat-shaped bread topped with cheese and egg.

capital-chn.summary: An East Asian country with a population of more than 1.4 billion. The capital is Beijing.
facts: Beijing is home to the Forbidden City, where the Ming and Qing emperors lived.
The Great Wall of China runs along the mountain ridges north of Beijing.

capital-kaz.summary: The world's largest landlocked country, where the nomadic tradition of hunting with golden eagles lives on. The capital is Astana.
facts: The capital moved from Almaty in 1997 and, after several name changes, is once again called Astana.
The Baikonur Cosmodrome is on its territory.

capital-qat.summary: A peninsula nation jutting into the Persian Gulf, home to the Arab broadcaster Al Jazeera. The capital is Doha.
facts: In 2022 it hosted the first World Cup in the Middle East, held in November and December to avoid the heat.
The gas field beneath its waters, shared with a neighboring country, is the largest in the world.

capital-khm.summary: A country in Indochina where, in the rainy season, a river reverses its flow and a lake swells to several times its size. The capital is Phnom Penh.
facts: Angkor Wat is a temple built by the Khmer Empire in the 12th century.
Angkor Wat appears in the center of its flag.

capital-kwt.summary: An oil-producing country at the northern end of the Persian Gulf whose dinar is the world's highest-valued currency. The capital is the city that shares the country's name.
facts: The Gulf War broke out after Iraq invaded in 1990.
As Iraqi forces retreated in 1991, they set fire to more than 600 oil wells.

capital-kgz.summary: A landlocked country in the Tian Shan whose flag shows the round roof frame of a nomad's yurt. The capital is Bishkek.
facts: The Tian Shan mountains cover more than 80 percent of the country.
Issyk-Kul is the second-largest mountain lake after South America's Lake Titicaca.

capital-tjk.summary: A landlocked country in the Pamir Mountains that, unlike its Turkic neighbors, speaks a Persian language. The capital is Dushanbe.
facts: More than 90 percent of the country is mountainous.
Its highest peak, Ismoil Somoni Peak, rises to 7,495 meters (24,590 feet).

capital-tha.summary: The land of tom yum soup and its famous kickboxing, and the only kingdom in Southeast Asia never colonized. The capital is Bangkok.
facts: Bangkok's full ceremonial name has 168 letters, earning it a Guinness record as the world's longest place name.
The Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha stand in the heart of the city.

capital-tkm.summary: A landlocked country east of the Caspian Sea whose capital, packed with white marble buildings, made it into Guinness World Records. The capital is Ashgabat.
facts: Most of the country is covered by the Karakum Desert.
The burning gas crater at Darvaza is known as the "Gates of Hell."

capital-tur.summary: A country spanning Asia and Europe that draws travelers with the hot-air balloons of Cappadocia and its kebabs. The capital is Ankara.
facts: Its largest city, Istanbul, was once Constantinople.
The Bosporus Strait separates the two continents.

capital-pak.summary: A country in the Indus River basin where pink Himalayan salt is mined. The capital is Islamabad.
facts: The capital moved from Karachi to Rawalpindi and then to this newly built city in the 1960s.
K2, the world's second-highest peak, stands in the Karakoram range in the north.

capital-pse.summary: A nation on the West Bank of the Jordan River that includes Bethlehem, said to be the birthplace of Jesus. Its administrative center is Ramallah.
facts: It claims East Jerusalem as its capital, but its government is based in Ramallah.
It became a UN non-member observer state in 2012 but is not yet a full member.

capital-phl.summary: A nation of more than 7,000 islands that draws many language students because English is an official language. The capital is Manila.
facts: Under Spanish rule, Manila was a hub of Asian trade.
Intramuros is the old walled city that survives in Manila.

capital-kor.summary: A country on the southern half of the Korean Peninsula that made its name worldwide with K-pop, TV dramas, and semiconductors. The capital is Seoul.
facts: Seoul, on the Han River, has been the capital for more than 600 years, since the Joseon dynasty.
Hangul Day on October 9 commemorates the proclamation of the Korean alphabet, Hunminjeongeum, in 1446.

capital-hkg.summary: A special administrative region ruled by Britain from 1842 until it was handed back to China in 1997.
facts: After the handover, "one country, two systems" was guaranteed for 50 years, until 2047.
It has more skyscrapers than any other city in the world.

capital-ggy.summary: A British Crown Dependency island in the western Channel Islands. The capital is St. Peter Port.
facts: It belongs to the British Crown but does not follow the laws of mainland Britain.
Victor Hugo finished “Les Misérables” in his house on the island while in exile.

capital-grc.summary: A country at the southern tip of the Balkan Peninsula with thousands of islands, including Santorini and its whitewashed houses. The capital is Athens.
facts: The Parthenon stands on the Acropolis hill.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

capital-nld.summary: A low-lying land on the North Sea that brings to mind windmills, tulips, and bicycles. The capital is Amsterdam.
facts: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital, but the government and parliament sit in The Hague.
In 1653 one of its sailors, Hendrick Hamel, was shipwrecked on Jeju Island and later wrote an account of his years in Korea.

capital-nor.summary: A country in western Scandinavia that grew rich from salmon farming and North Sea oil. The capital is Oslo.
facts: The Sognefjord, more than 200 kilometers (124 miles) long, is the country's longest fjord.
The Nobel Peace Prize is the only Nobel Prize awarded in Oslo.

capital-dnk.summary: A country of the Jutland Peninsula and many islands, the homeland of Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tales. The capital is Copenhagen.
facts: LEGO toys got their start in the town of Billund in 1932.
Greenland is one of its autonomous territories.

capital-deu.summary: The home of the Oktoberfest beer festival and the Autobahn, with stretches that have no speed limit. The capital is Berlin.
facts: Berlin became the capital with reunification in 1990, and the government moved there from Bonn in 1999.
The Berlin Wall went up in 1961 and fell in 1989.

capital-lva.summary: The middle of the three Baltic states, with a tradition of song festivals where tens of thousands sing together. The capital is Riga.
facts: The old town of Riga, a Hanseatic city founded in 1201, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
One in three buildings in central Riga is Art Nouveau.

capital-rus.summary: The home of the ballet “Swan Lake” and matryoshka dolls, and the largest country in the world by area. The capital is Moscow.
facts: It spans Europe and Asia and has eleven time zones.
The Trans-Siberian Railway runs 9,289 kilometers (5,772 miles) from Moscow to Vladivostok.

capital-rou.summary: An Eastern European country ringed by the Carpathian Mountains, whose language descends from Latin. The capital is Bucharest.
facts: The region of Transylvania is the setting of the Dracula story.
It has the delta where the Danube flows into the Black Sea.

capital-lux.summary: A Western European grand duchy that in 2020 became the first country to make all public transportation free nationwide. Its capital shares the country's name.
facts: The country and its capital share the same name, and Luxembourgish, French, and German are all used.
The Court of Justice of the European Union and the European Investment Bank are headquartered in its capital.

capital-ltu.summary: The southernmost of the three Baltic states, so crazy about basketball that its men's team has won Olympic bronze three times. The capital is Vilnius.
facts: In the 15th century, as a grand duchy, its lands stretched from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea.
Countless crosses are planted on the Hill of Crosses.

capital-lie.summary: An Alpine principality on the Rhine that has won all 10 of its Olympic medals in alpine skiing. The capital is Vaduz.
facts: Along with Uzbekistan, it is one of only two doubly landlocked countries.
It abolished its army in 1868 and has had no military since.

capital-imn.summary: A British Crown Dependency between Great Britain and Ireland. The capital is Douglas.
facts: Its flag features a symbol of three interlocking legs.
Since 1907, the island has closed its public roads to host the TT motorcycle races.

capital-mco.summary: A city-state on the Mediterranean coast, home to the Monte Carlo casino. The whole country is a single city.
facts: At about 2 square kilometers (0.8 square miles), it is the second-smallest country after Vatican City and the most densely populated.
Every year a car race is held right through its city streets.

capital-mne.summary: A small Adriatic country where the medieval walled town of Kotor sits deep inside a bay. The capital is Podgorica.
facts: Its name means "black mountain," after Mount Lovćen, thickly covered with evergreen forest.
It became independent in 2006 after splitting from Serbia.

capital-mda.summary: A small landlocked Eastern European country whose territory east of the Dniester River has broken away. The capital is Chișinău.
facts: In 2023 it changed the official name of its language from Moldovan to Romanian.
In 2005 the Milestii Mici wine cellars entered Guinness World Records as the world's largest wine collection.

capital-mlt.summary: An island nation in the middle of the Mediterranean whose official languages are English and a native tongue with Arabic roots. The capital is Valletta.
facts: In 1565 the Knights of Malta held off the Great Siege by the Ottoman Empire.
In 1980 the entire city of Valletta was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

capital-vat.summary: The center of the Catholic Church, surrounded by the city of Rome. It is a city-state where the pope resides.
facts: Michelangelo's Genesis frescoes cover the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
The Swiss Guard has protected the pope for more than 500 years.

capital-bel.summary: A small Western European country lined with shops selling fries, waffles, and chocolate. The capital is Brussels.
facts: Many of the European Union's main institutions are based in Brussels.
Hergé, creator of the comic “The Adventures of Tintin,” was born in Brussels.

capital-blr.summary: A landlocked Eastern European country that builds BelAZ, giant dump trucks for mining. The capital is Minsk.
facts: Its name means "White Rus'," and before independence in 1991 it was known as Byelorussia.
European bison live in the primeval Białowieża Forest, which extends into Poland.

capital-bih.summary: A Balkan country with a tradition of diving into the river from the old stone bridge in Mostar. The capital is Sarajevo.
facts: The 1914 assassination in Sarajevo triggered World War I.
Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics.

capital-mkd.summary: A landlocked Balkan country where Mother Teresa was born, in the city that is now its capital. The capital is Skopje.
facts: In 2019 it changed its name by adding "North."
Lake Ohrid, millions of years old and one of the oldest lakes in Europe, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

capital-bgr.summary: A country in the eastern Balkans whose name appears in the scientific name of a yogurt bacterium. The capital is Sofia.
facts: Rose oil for perfume is distilled in the Rose Valley of Kazanlak.
The Cyrillic alphabet spread outward from this land.

capital-smr.summary: A tiny republic atop Mount Titano, surrounded on all sides by a neighboring country. It issues commemorative stamps and coins for sale.
facts: It is often considered the oldest surviving republic in the world.
Each peak of Mount Titano is crowned by an old tower.

capital-srb.summary: A landlocked country in the central Balkans that produced tennis star Novak Djokovic. The capital is Belgrade.
facts: The city grew up where the Sava River meets the Danube.
Belgrade was the capital of the former Yugoslavia and is home to the House of Flowers, where Tito is buried.

capital-sjm.summary: An Arctic Ocean archipelago where you can't leave town without gear to fend off polar bears. The main settlement is Longyearbyen.
facts: In 2002 South Korea opened its Dasan Arctic research station at Ny-Ålesund.
A vault storing seeds from around the world is located here.

capital-swe.summary: A country in eastern Scandinavia that gave the world IKEA, Volvo, and the pop group ABBA. The capital is Stockholm.
facts: Spread across fourteen islands, the city is known as a city on the water.
Every Nobel Prize ceremony except the Peace Prize is held in Stockholm.

capital-che.summary: A landlocked Alpine country that holds national referendums four times a year. The city that serves as its capital is Bern.
facts: Its constitution names no capital; Bern is designated the "federal city."
Geneva hosts the UN's European headquarters and the headquarters of the International Committee of the Red Cross.

capital-esp.summary: An Iberian country of paella, flamenco, and the soccer powerhouse Real Madrid. The capital is Madrid.
facts: Madrid sits on a plateau in the very center of the peninsula.
In 2025 Barcelona's Sagrada Família became the tallest church in the world.

capital-svk.summary: A landlocked Central European country that makes more cars per person than any other nation. The capital is Bratislava.
facts: Bratislava is the only capital that borders two other countries.
From 1536 to 1783 it was the capital of the Kingdom of Hungary.

capital-svn.summary: A small country at the southern edge of the Alps where a little train runs through the limestone Postojna Cave. The capital is Ljubljana.
facts: A small island with a church sits in the middle of Lake Bled.
Forests cover 58 percent of the country, the most in the EU after Finland and Sweden.

capital-isl.summary: A volcanic island nation in the North Atlantic, home to Geysir, the hot spring that gave English the word "geyser." The capital is Reykjavík.
facts: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of any sovereign state.
Geothermal energy heats 90 percent of homes, and all electricity comes from hydropower and geothermal sources.

capital-irl.summary: The home of Guinness stout and Celtic music, covering most of the southern part of its island. The capital is Dublin.
facts: The northeast of the island is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom.
On St. Patrick's Day, March 17, people dress in green and march in parades.

capital-and.summary: A tiny principality in the high valleys of the Pyrenees. Catalan is its only official language.
facts: The President of France and the Bishop of Urgell in Spain jointly serve as heads of state.
Low taxes draw many tourists for duty-free shopping and skiing.

capital-alb.summary: A country on the eastern shore of the Adriatic whose flag bears a black double-headed eagle. The capital is Tirana.
facts: In 1967 it became the first country in the world to declare itself an atheist state.
Under Hoxha's regime, more than 170,000 concrete bunkers were built by 1983.

capital-est.summary: A country on the eastern Baltic Sea whose developers created the internet calling service Skype. The capital is Tallinn.
facts: Tallinn's old town preserves its medieval look remarkably well.
In 2005 it became the first country to use online voting in a legally binding election.

capital-gbr.summary: A kingdom on the island of Great Britain and the northern part of the island of Ireland, where the rules of modern soccer were first written. The capital is London.
facts: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland together make up one country.
Big Ben is the name of the great bell inside the clock tower of the Houses of Parliament.

capital-aut.summary: A landlocked country in the eastern Alps, home to Salzburg, the setting of “The Sound of Music.” The capital is Vienna.
facts: Vienna is a city of music where Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and Ludwig van Beethoven worked.
The cream-topped coffee known in Korea as "Vienna coffee" is Vienna's Einspänner.

capital-ala.summary: A cluster of islands at the mouth of the Gulf of Bothnia in the Baltic Sea. The capital is Mariehamn.
facts: It is an autonomous region of Finland where Swedish is spoken.
It is a neutral zone where a treaty prohibits military forces.

capital-ukr.summary: An Eastern European country that brings to mind endless sunflower fields and red borscht soup. The capital is Kyiv.
facts: Its vast black-soil lands earned it the name "breadbasket of Europe."
The Dnipro River divides the country into east and west.

capital-ita.summary: A boot-shaped peninsula nation, home of pizza, pasta, and Renaissance art. The capital is Rome.
facts: Vatican City is a separate state in the middle of Rome.
The Colosseum is an amphitheater of ancient Rome.

capital-jey.summary: The largest of the Channel Islands, a British Crown Dependency. The capital is St. Helier.
facts: As a Crown Dependency, it issues its own money and stamps.
The Jersey cow, a breed that gives rich, yellowish milk, originated on this island.

capital-gib.summary: A British Overseas Territory on a rocky headland at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula. The whole territory is a single city.
facts: It guards the strait where Europe and Africa come closest together.
The Rock is home to the only wild monkeys in Europe.

capital-cze.summary: A landlocked Central European country where golden Pilsner lager was first brewed. The capital is Prague.
facts: In 1993 it split peacefully from Slovakia.
Prague Castle and the Charles Bridge stand along the Vltava River.

capital-unk.summary: A landlocked country in the central Balkans that uses the euro despite being outside the European Union. The capital is Pristina.
facts: It declared independence from Serbia in 2008, and South Korea recognized it that March.
Not every country recognizes it as a state yet.

capital-hrv.summary: An Adriatic coastal country where the cravat, the forerunner of the necktie, originated. The capital is Zagreb.
facts: The Walls of Dubrovnik were a filming location for the TV series “Game of Thrones.”
It gained independence from Yugoslavia in the early 1990s.

capital-cyp.summary: An island nation in the eastern Mediterranean where Aphrodite, goddess of love, is said to have been born from the waves. The capital is Nicosia.
facts: The island is divided into north and south, and the dividing line runs through Nicosia itself.
Geographically it is closer to Asia, but it is a member of the European Union.

capital-fro.summary: A North Atlantic archipelago where sheep outnumber people. The capital is Tórshavn.
facts: An autonomous territory of Denmark, it is made up of eighteen islands.
With almost no trees, grass-covered roofs are common.

capital-prt.summary: A country at the western edge of the Iberian Peninsula, home of the egg tart pastel de nata. The capital is Lisbon.
facts: The Korean word for bread, ppang, came from the Portuguese word pão by way of Japan.
Lisbon had to be rebuilt after the great earthquake of 1755.

capital-pol.summary: A Central European country where the site of Auschwitz, the camp built by the Nazis, still stands. The capital is Warsaw.
facts: Warsaw's Old Town, destroyed in World War II, was rebuilt just as it had been.
In 2022 it bought large numbers of South Korean K2 tanks and K9 self-propelled howitzers.

capital-fra.summary: The land of baguettes, cheese, and wine, where a bicycle race circles the country every July. The capital is Paris.
facts: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair.
The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre.

capital-fin.summary: A Northern European country, the home of the sauna and the phone maker Nokia. The capital is Helsinki.
facts: With more than 180,000 lakes, it is called the land of a thousand lakes.
Xylitol chewing gum was first made here in 1975.

capital-hun.summary: A landlocked Central European country, birthplace of Ernő Rubik, inventor of the Rubik's Cube. The capital is Budapest.
facts: In 1873 the three towns of Buda, Óbuda, and Pest merged to form today's capital.
Goulash, a stew of meat seasoned with paprika, began as a herdsmen's soup.

capital-gha.summary: A West African nation on the Gulf of Guinea that was called the Gold Coast in colonial times. The capital is Accra.
facts: Gaining independence in 1957, it was the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to become a nation.
Lotte's Ghana chocolate, a popular Korean brand, is said to be named after this cocoa-producing country.

capital-gab.summary: An equatorial country with more than 85 percent of its land covered by forest. The capital is Libreville.
facts: Albert Schweitzer opened a hospital in Lambaréné in 1913.
In 2002 it set aside about one-tenth of its territory as 13 national parks.

capital-gmb.summary: A West African riverside country depicted in the novel “Roots” as the homeland of its hero, Kunta Kinte. The capital is Banjul.
facts: It stretches long and narrow along the Gambia River and is surrounded by Senegal.
It is the smallest country on the African mainland.

capital-gin.summary: A West African country on the Atlantic coast that voted for immediate independence in a 1958 referendum. The capital is Conakry.
facts: The Niger River rises in its highlands.
It has the world's largest reserves of bauxite, the raw material for aluminum, about a quarter of the global total.

capital-gnb.summary: A West African country on the Atlantic coast where cashew nuts make up about 90 percent of exports. The capital is Bissau.
facts: It declared independence in 1973, and Portugal recognized it in 1974.
Dozens of islands of the Bijagós Archipelago are scattered off its coast.

capital-nam.summary: A country where the Namib Desert stretches along the Atlantic coast. The capital is Windhoek.
facts: It gained independence from South African rule in 1990.
It is the second most sparsely populated country after Mongolia.

capital-nga.summary: Africa's most populous country, which built the Nollywood film industry. The capital is Abuja.
facts: In 1991 the capital moved from Lagos to Abuja.
At the 2010 World Cup it drew 2–2 with South Korea, sending South Korea to its first-ever Round of 16 on foreign soil.

capital-ssd.summary: The world's newest country, where the vast Sudd wetlands of the Nile spread out. The capital is Juba.
facts: It became independent from Sudan in 2011.
The White Nile runs through the country from south to north, and the capital, Juba, sits on its banks.

capital-zaf.summary: A country at the southern tip of Africa, where Mandela ended apartheid and became president. The executive capital is Pretoria.
facts: Pretoria is the executive capital, Cape Town the legislative capital, and Bloemfontein the judicial capital.
In 2010 it hosted the first World Cup held in Africa.

capital-ner.summary: A landlocked country south of the Sahara where the mud-brick minaret of the Agadez Mosque rises. The capital is Niamey.
facts: The Niger River passes through the southwest, and the capital, Niamey, lies on its banks.
Nigersaurus, a dinosaur with a broad, vacuum-cleaner-like snout, is named after this country.

capital-lbr.summary: A West African country on the Atlantic coast where many of the world's cargo ships are registered on paper. The capital is Monrovia.
facts: It was founded by freed American slaves who crossed the ocean.
The capital is named after U.S. President James Monroe.

capital-lso.summary: A mountain kingdom in the interior of southern Africa, where people wrap themselves in Basotho blankets and ride ponies. The capital is Maseru.
facts: It is completely surrounded by South Africa.
Even its lowest point is 1,400 meters (4,593 feet) above sea level, the highest low point of any country.

capital-reu.summary: A volcanic island in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar. Its main town is Saint-Denis.
facts: As an overseas region of France, it uses the euro.
Piton de la Fournaise is one of the most frequently erupting volcanoes.

capital-rwa.summary: A small landlocked East African country whose streets are spotless thanks to a plastic bag ban since 2008. The capital is Kigali.
facts: Its many hills have earned it the name "land of a thousand hills."
It has a volcanoes national park where mountain gorillas live.

capital-lby.summary: A North African desert country with the ruins of Leptis Magna, a city of the Roman era. The capital is Tripoli.
facts: It built the Great Man-Made River, a network of pipes that carries water from beneath the Sahara to coastal cities.
Most of its people live in a narrow strip along the Mediterranean.

capital-mdg.summary: A large island nation in the Indian Ocean off the east coast of Africa, and a leading producer of vanilla. The capital is Antananarivo.
facts: Six of the eight species of baobab tree grow only on this island.
It is the world's fourth-largest island, after Greenland, New Guinea, and Borneo.

capital-myt.summary: An island in the Mozambique Channel nicknamed the "perfume island" for its ylang-ylang flowers. Its main town is Mamoudzou.
facts: In a 1974 vote, unlike the other islands of the Comoros, it chose to remain with France.
The lagoon inside the coral reef encircling the island is exceptionally large.

capital-mwi.summary: A landlocked country in southeastern Africa whose lake's colorful cichlids are sold worldwide as aquarium fish. The capital is Lilongwe.
facts: Lake Malawi covers a fifth of the country.
Lake Malawi is about 365 miles long, earning it the nickname “Calendar Lake.”

capital-mli.summary: A landlocked West African country home to the Great Mosque of Djenné, built of mud brick. The capital is Bamako.
facts: In the 14th century, King Mansa Musa handed out so much gold on his pilgrimage to Mecca that gold prices in Cairo fell.
Timbuktu was a center of trans-Saharan trade and learning.

capital-mar.summary: A kingdom at Africa's northwestern tip that greets travelers with spice markets, mint tea and tagines. The capital is Rabat.
facts: It faces Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar.
The old medinas of Marrakesh and Fez are World Heritage Sites.

capital-mus.summary: An Indian Ocean resort island nation of sugarcane fields and coral-reef lagoons. The capital is Port Louis.
facts: It was home to the dodo, a flightless bird.
It was uninhabited until the Dutch settled there in 1638.

capital-mrt.summary: A desert country in northwestern Africa on the Atlantic coast. The capital is Nouakchott.
facts: Much of the octopus imported into South Korea comes from here.
Iron-ore trains up to 3 kilometers long travel 704 kilometers across the desert.

capital-moz.summary: A Portuguese-speaking country on the Indian Ocean coast of southeastern Africa. The capital is Maputo.
facts: The Mozambique Channel separates it from Madagascar.
Its flag features an AK-47 rifle alongside a book and a hoe.

capital-ben.summary: A long, narrow West African country on the Gulf of Guinea. The capital is Porto-Novo.
facts: Porto-Novo is the official capital, but Cotonou is the real center of the country.
Vodun, the root of Voodoo, is an officially recognized religion, and January 10 is Vodun Day.

capital-bwa.summary: A landlocked southern African country with more elephants than anywhere else in Africa. The capital is Gaborone.
facts: The Okavango Delta never reaches the sea; its waters dry up in the desert instead.
The Orapa mine, discovered in 1967, is the world's largest diamond mine by area.

capital-bdi.summary: A small landlocked East African country whose royal drum dance is recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. The capital is Gitega.
facts: In 2019 the capital moved from Bujumbura to Gitega.
The former capital, Bujumbura, lies on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, the world's second-deepest lake.

capital-bfa.summary: A landlocked West African country that hosts FESPACO, Africa's biennial film festival. The capital is Ouagadougou.
facts: Its name means “land of upright people.”
In 1984 it changed its name from Upper Volta.

capital-stp.summary: A tiny island nation in the Gulf of Guinea once known as the “Chocolate Islands.” The capital shares its name with the larger of its two main islands.
facts: The equator passes over Rolas Islet in the south.
From 1905 to 1911 it was the world's largest cocoa producer.

capital-esh.summary: A desert territory on Africa's northwestern Atlantic coast whose sovereignty has been disputed for more than 50 years. The capital is Laayoune.
facts: A 2,700-kilometer sand berm built by Morocco splits the territory in two.
In 2025 the UN Security Council endorsed Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for negotiations for the first time.

capital-sen.summary: The westernmost country of mainland Africa, whose capital gave its name to the Dakar Rally. The capital is Dakar.
facts: Gorée Island preserves the painful history of the slave trade.
In the opening match of the 2002 World Cup, co-hosted by South Korea and Japan, it beat defending champion France 1–0.

capital-syc.summary: An Indian Ocean nation of 115 scattered islands. The capital is Victoria.
facts: With just over 100,000 people, it is Africa's least populous country.
The coco de mer seed can weigh up to 25 kilograms, making it the largest seed of any plant.

capital-shn.summary: A remote British Overseas Territory in the middle of the South Atlantic. The capital is Jamestown.
facts: Napoleon was exiled to this island and died there.
Lying in the middle of the Atlantic, it didn't get regular flights until 2017.

capital-som.summary: A Horn of Africa country whose waters South Korea's Cheonghae Unit was deployed to protect from pirates. The capital is Mogadishu.
facts: It has the longest coastline in mainland Africa.
It borders both the Indian Ocean and the Gulf of Aden, and the shipping lane to the Suez Canal passes just offshore.

capital-sdn.summary: A country on the upper Nile that produces much of the gum arabic used in colas and candy. The capital is Khartoum.
facts: The Blue Nile and the White Nile meet at Khartoum.
More than 200 Nubian pyramids survive at Meroë and other sites, more than in Egypt.

capital-sle.summary: A West African country on the Atlantic that early navigators named the “Lion Mountains.” The capital is Freetown.
facts: Freed slaves settled here, so the capital was named the “city of freedom.”
From 1991 to 2002 it suffered a civil war fought over diamonds.

capital-dza.summary: The land of raï music and couscous, and the largest country in Africa by area. The capital is Algiers.
facts: More than 80 percent of the country is Sahara.
After nearly eight years of war, it won independence from France in 1962.

capital-ago.summary: A country on Africa's southwestern Atlantic coast where oil makes up most exports. The capital is Luanda.
facts: Right after gaining independence from Portugal in 1975, it plunged into a 27-year civil war that lasted until 2002.
The partner dance kizomba emerged here around 1980 and spread around the world.

capital-eri.summary: A Red Sea country where espresso and pasta, introduced in colonial times, are still part of daily life. The capital is Asmara.
facts: It won independence from Ethiopia in 1993.
Asmara's 1930s modernist buildings became a World Heritage Site in 2017.

capital-swz.summary: A landlocked southern African kingdom where tens of thousands gather every year for Umhlanga, the Reed Dance festival. The capital is Mbabane.
facts: In 2018 it changed its name from Swaziland.
It is Africa's last remaining absolute monarchy.

capital-eth.summary: A highland country in eastern Africa that uses its own calendar with 13 months in a year. The capital is Addis Ababa.
facts: The arabica coffee plant originated in its southwestern highlands.
The African Union is headquartered in Addis Ababa.

capital-uga.summary: A landlocked country on Lake Victoria that Winston Churchill called the “Pearl of Africa.” The capital is Kampala.
facts: The Nile flows out of Lake Victoria.
The equator crosses the south of the country, and an equator marker stands beside the road from Kampala to Masaka.

capital-egy.summary: The country where an ancient civilization of pharaohs, mummies and hieroglyphs flourished along the Nile. The capital is Cairo.
facts: In November 2025 the Grand Egyptian Museum opened next to the pyramids.
The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

capital-zmb.summary: A landlocked southern African country that lives off the Copperbelt, its cluster of copper mines. The capital is Lusaka.
facts: Victoria Falls lies on its border with Zimbabwe.
Its name comes from the Zambezi River.

capital-gnq.summary: A west-central African country split between the volcanic island of Bioko and a mainland territory. The capital is Ciudad de la Paz.
facts: In January 2026 the capital moved from Malabo, on the island, to the mainland.
It is one of the few countries in Africa with Spanish as an official language.

capital-caf.summary: A landlocked African country north of the equator, home to the Dzanga-Sangha reserve where forest elephants gather. The capital is Bangui.
facts: In 1977 Bokassa crowned himself emperor in a stadium in Bangui.
It has diamonds and gold but has been torn by long civil wars.

capital-dji.summary: A small country at the mouth of the Red Sea in the northern Horn of Africa. Its capital shares the country's name.
facts: U.S., French, Chinese and Japanese military bases are all near the capital.
Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa.

capital-zwe.summary: A landlocked southern African country where inflation once soared so high it printed a 100-trillion-dollar banknote. The capital is Harare.
facts: It is named after Great Zimbabwe, an ancient city built of stone.
It shares Victoria Falls with Zambia.

capital-tcd.summary: A landlocked country in the heart of Africa, where the volcanic Tibesti Mountains rise from the Sahara in the north. The capital is N'Djamena.
facts: Drought and irrigation that draws on its rivers have shrunk Lake Chad dramatically since the 1960s.
Emi Koussi in the Tibesti Mountains is the highest peak in the Sahara.

capital-cmr.summary: A country at the inner corner of the Gulf of Guinea that produced soccer star Samuel Eto'o. The capital is Yaoundé.
facts: With desert, savanna and rainforest, it is called “Africa in miniature.”
Both French and English are official languages.

capital-cpv.summary: An island nation off West Africa that was once a way station in the Atlantic slave trade. The capital is Praia.
facts: It is made up of ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic.
The “Barefoot Diva,” Cesária Évora, brought morna music to the world.

capital-ken.summary: An East African country on the equator that exports large amounts of tea and flowers to Europe. The capital is Nairobi.
facts: The Great Migration of wildlife can be seen on the Maasai Mara plains.
In 2019 Eliud Kipchoge broke the two-hour marathon barrier in an unofficial race.

capital-com.summary: An island nation at the northern entrance to the Mozambique Channel whose Arabic name means “islands of the moon.” The capital is Moroni.
facts: The country is made up of three islands in the Indian Ocean.
It is the world's top producer of ylang-ylang, a flower used in Chanel No. 5.

capital-civ.summary: A Gulf of Guinea country home to the Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, a vast church modeled on St. Peter's Basilica. The capital is Yamoussoukro.
facts: Yamoussoukro is the official capital, but Abidjan is the de facto center.
It is considered the world's largest cocoa producer.

capital-cog.summary: A west-central African country straddling the equator, with rainforest covering nearly two-thirds of its land. The capital is Brazzaville.
facts: Its capital faces Kinshasa across the river, making them the world's two closest capitals.
In 2021 it had Congolese rumba inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage together with its neighbor across the river.

capital-cod.summary: A huge country in the middle of Africa that mines much of the cobalt used in phone batteries. The capital is Kinshasa.
facts: With depths of more than 220 meters, the Congo River is the deepest river in the world.
It is Africa's second-largest country, after Algeria.

capital-tza.summary: A country formed in 1964 when Tanganyika and Zanzibar merged. The capital is Dodoma.
facts: It is home to Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak.
Freddie Mercury, the lead singer of Queen, was born on Zanzibar.

capital-tgo.summary: A Gulf of Guinea country that South Korea beat at the 2006 World Cup for its first-ever World Cup win on foreign soil. The capital is Lomé.
facts: Its coastline is only 56 kilometers long, yet the country stretches more than 500 kilometers from north to south.
Mining and exporting phosphate is a major industry.

capital-tun.summary: A North African country where a village used for the desert-planet scenes in “Star Wars” still stands. The capital is Tunis.
facts: It was home to ancient Carthage, birthplace of Hannibal, which fell to Rome in 146 BC.
Both the Sahara and the Mediterranean lie within its borders.

capital-guy.summary: A country in northeastern South America whose economy has boomed since a huge offshore oil discovery in 2015. The capital is Georgetown.
facts: It is the only country on the South American mainland with English as an official language.
Kaieteur Falls drops 226 meters in a single plunge, about four times the height of Niagara Falls.

capital-glp.summary: A Caribbean island in the Lesser Antilles that produces bananas and rum. The capital is Basseterre.
facts: It consists of two islands shaped like butterfly wings, joined by a narrow channel.
It is an overseas department of France in the Caribbean.

capital-gtm.summary: A Central American country where descendants of the Maya make up a large share of the population. Its capital shares the country's name.
facts: Tikal is a Maya ruin deep in the rainforest.
Volcanoes make earthquakes common, and after the great earthquake of 1773 the capital was moved away from the old capital, Antigua.

capital-grd.summary: An island nation at the southern end of the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean. The capital is St. George's.
facts: Nutmeg grows so abundantly that it appears on the flag, earning the country the nickname “Spice Isle.”
In 2006 the world's first underwater sculpture park opened off its west coast.

capital-grl.summary: A vast island of ice between the Arctic Ocean and the North Atlantic. The capital is Nuuk.
facts: It is the world's largest island and an autonomous territory of Denmark.
More than 80 percent of its land is covered by ice.

capital-nic.summary: The largest country in Central America by area. The capital is Managua.
facts: Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America.
The volcanic island of Ometepe sits in the middle of the lake.

capital-dom.summary: The country on the eastern side of Hispaniola, where merengue and bachata were born. The capital is Santo Domingo.
facts: Santo Domingo is one of the oldest European-founded cities in the Americas.
It sends more players to Major League Baseball than any country except the United States.

capital-dma.summary: A volcanic island nation between Guadeloupe and Martinique. The capital is Roseau.
facts: Thick with volcanoes and forests, it is known as the “Nature Island of the Caribbean.”
Boiling Lake, in its mountains, is the second-largest boiling lake in the world.

capital-mtq.summary: An overseas department of France in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean. The capital is Fort-de-France.
facts: In 1902 Mount Pelée erupted and wiped out Saint-Pierre, then the island's main city.
Napoleon's first empress, Joséphine, was born on this island.

capital-mex.summary: A country in southern North America known for tacos, tequila and the Day of the Dead. Its capital shares the country's name.
facts: The capital was built on the site of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital.
At the 2026 World Cup, South Korea played its group-stage matches in Guadalajara and Monterrey.

capital-msr.summary: A small volcanic British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. The capital is Plymouth.
facts: The volcano awoke in 1995, and in 1997 the capital, Plymouth, was abandoned.
Today Brades in the north serves as the interim capital, and a new capital is being built at Little Bay.

capital-usa.summary: A federal nation of 50 states in North America. The capital is Washington, D.C.
facts: The capital is a special district that belongs to no state.
The $1 bill features George Washington, the first president and the capital's namesake.

capital-vir.summary: American-owned islands in the Caribbean at the eastern end of the Greater Antilles. The capital is Charlotte Amalie.
facts: In 1917 the United States bought them from Denmark for $25 million in gold.
Although they are U.S. territory, cars drive on the left.

capital-brb.summary: An island nation sitting alone at the eastern edge of the Caribbean. The capital is Bridgetown.
facts: In 2021 it removed the British monarch as head of state and became a republic.
It is the island where singer Rihanna was born and raised.

capital-bhs.summary: A northern Caribbean island nation that includes the island where Christopher Columbus first landed in 1492. The capital is Nassau.
facts: It is made up of more than 700 islands and cays.
Big Major Cay, home to swimming pigs, is a popular attraction.

capital-bmu.summary: An isolated British Overseas Territory in the western North Atlantic. The capital is Hamilton.
facts: Knee-length shorts are named after the island, and here they count as business attire.
White stepped roofs collect rainwater for drinking.

capital-ven.summary: A northern South American country named “Little Venice” after houses built over the water. The capital is Caracas.
facts: It is home to Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall.
It has the largest proven oil reserves in the world.

capital-blz.summary: A Central American country on the Caribbean coast, home to Maya ruins and coral reefs. The capital is Belmopan.
facts: It is the only country in Central America with English as an official language.
Offshore lies the Great Blue Hole, a deep-blue sinkhole in the sea.

capital-bol.summary: A landlocked Andean country with a large Indigenous population, on the shores of Lake Titicaca. The constitutional capital is Sucre.
facts: La Paz, the seat of government, sits more than 3,600 meters above sea level.
The Uyuni salt flat is known as a mirror that reflects the sky.

capital-bra.summary: The largest country in South America, famous for its samba carnival. The capital is Brasília.
facts: In 1960 the capital moved from Rio de Janeiro to Brasília.
Rainforest in the Amazon River basin covers the north of the country.

capital-maf.summary: A French overseas collectivity on the northern part of a Caribbean island. The capital is Marigot.
facts: It is the northern side of an island shared by France and the Netherlands.
There are almost no border checks, so people simply walk across.

capital-blm.summary: A small French overseas collectivity in the Caribbean. The capital is Gustavia.
facts: It belonged to Sweden for 94 years starting in 1784, which is why the capital is named after a Swedish king.
It is one of the Caribbean's most exclusive luxury destinations.

capital-spm.summary: A group of French islands south of Newfoundland, Canada. The capital shares its name with the main island.
facts: It is the only part of the former New France still under French rule.
It is one of the few places in North America that uses the euro.

capital-lca.summary: A volcanic island nation in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean. The capital is Castries.
facts: The two Pitons, rising straight out of the sea, are the island's symbol.
It has produced two Nobel laureates, earning a Guinness record for the most per capita.

capital-vct.summary: An island nation in the southern Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean. The capital is Kingstown.
facts: It consists of a main island and just over 30 smaller islands.
The first “Pirates of the Caribbean” film was shot at Wallilabou Bay on the main island.

capital-kna.summary: An independent nation made up of two Caribbean islands. The capital is Basseterre.
facts: It is the smallest country in the Americas.
In 1623 the first English colony in the Caribbean was founded here.

capital-sur.summary: A small country in northeastern South America where descendants of many Asian and African peoples live side by side. The capital is Paramaribo.
facts: It is the only country in South America with Dutch as an official language.
More than 90 percent of the country is covered by forest.

capital-sxm.summary: A constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands on the southern part of a Caribbean island. The capital is Philipsburg.
facts: It is the Dutch side of an island shared with France.
At Maho Beach, airliners come in so low they seem to skim the heads of beachgoers.

capital-abw.summary: A southern Caribbean island where white-sand beaches line a dry, cactus-dotted landscape. The capital is Oranjestad.
facts: It lies outside the hurricane belt, so the weather is almost always fine.
In 1986 it split from the Netherlands Antilles to become a separate constituent country.

capital-arg.summary: A country in southern South America that produced soccer stars Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi. The capital is Buenos Aires.
facts: Asado, beef raised on the Pampas and grilled over charcoal, is the national dish.
The tango was born in the port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires.

capital-hti.summary: A Creole-speaking country on western Hispaniola with deep Vodou traditions. The capital is Port-au-Prince.
facts: In 1804 an uprising of enslaved people made it the first country in Latin America to win independence.
After the 2010 earthquake, South Korea's Danbi Unit went there to help with reconstruction.

capital-atg.summary: A two-island nation in the northern Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean. The capital is St. John's.
facts: It is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.
Cricket is the national sport, and West Indies batting legend Viv Richards comes from here.

capital-aia.summary: A British Overseas Territory in the northern Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean. The capital is The Valley.
facts: Its name comes from its long, eel-like shape.
Sales of .ai internet domains brought in nearly half of government revenue in 2025.

capital-ecu.summary: A country straddling the equator that exports large amounts of roses and bananas. The capital is Quito.
facts: Its name is Spanish for “equator.”
The Galápagos Islands belong to it.

capital-slv.summary: The smallest country in Central America. The capital is San Salvador.
facts: It is the only Central American country with a coastline solely on the Pacific.
In 2021 it became the first country to make Bitcoin legal tender, then dropped it in 2025.

capital-vgb.summary: A British Overseas Territory in the northern Lesser Antilles where hundreds of thousands of companies have their registered addresses. The capital is Road Town.
facts: It is made up of some 60 islands and cays.
It is famous for chartering yachts to sail between its islands.

capital-hnd.summary: The Central American country that gave rise to the term “banana republic.” The capital is Tegucigalpa.
facts: The ruins of Copán mark the southeastern edge of the Maya civilization.
It has coastlines on both the Caribbean and the Pacific.

capital-ury.summary: A small country in southeastern South America where people commonly carry thermoses for their mate tea. The capital is Montevideo.
facts: It hosted and won the first World Cup in 1930.
Most of the country is gently rolling grassland.

capital-jam.summary: A Caribbean island nation that grows Blue Mountain, a premium coffee. The capital is Kingston.
facts: Reggae was born on this island.
Usain Bolt set the 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds in 2009.

capital-chl.summary: An extremely long country running north to south that exports large amounts of wine and salmon. The capital is Santiago.
facts: The Atacama in the north is the driest desert outside the polar regions.
It was the first country to sign a free trade agreement (FTA) with South Korea.

capital-bes.summary: Three Dutch islands scattered across the Caribbean. The capital is Kralendijk.
facts: The name covers the three islands of Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba.
They are special municipalities of the Netherlands, yet they use the U.S. dollar instead of the euro.

capital-can.summary: The land of maple syrup and ice hockey, spanning much of northern North America. The capital is Ottawa.
facts: It is the second-largest country by area, after Russia.
The $1 coin shows a loon, a water bird, so it is called the “loonie.”

capital-cym.summary: A Caribbean British Overseas Territory with the white sands of Seven Mile Beach and world-class dive sites. The capital is Georgetown.
facts: With no income or corporate tax, it is a financial center that draws money from around the world.
At Stingray City, a shallow sandbar, you can swim with stingrays.

capital-cri.summary: A Central American country that draws ecotourists to see sloths and tropical forests. The capital is San José.
facts: It abolished its army in 1948 and redirected the defense budget to education and health care.
More than a quarter of its land is protected.

capital-col.summary: A country in northwestern South America that produces large amounts of emeralds and coffee. The capital is Bogotá.
facts: It was the only Latin American country to send combat troops to the Korean War.
Gabriel García Márquez, author of “One Hundred Years of Solitude,” was from here.

capital-cub.summary: A Caribbean island nation where 1950s classic cars cruise the streets and salsa music fills the air. The capital is Havana.
facts: Old Havana is a World Heritage Site.
Ernest Hemingway lived outside Havana and wrote “The Old Man and the Sea” there.

capital-cuw.summary: A constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in the Caribbean, off the northern coast of South America. The capital is Willemstad.
facts: Colorful Dutch-style buildings line its harbor.
The blue liqueur of the same name is made from the peels of the island's oranges.

capital-tca.summary: A British Overseas Territory in the Atlantic at the southeastern end of the Lucayan Archipelago. The capital is Cockburn Town.
facts: The islands have long produced salt by evaporating seawater.
Grace Bay Beach is often ranked among the best beaches in the world.

capital-tto.summary: A two-island nation in the Caribbean just off the South American mainland. The capital is Port of Spain.
facts: The steelpan, made from oil drums, was born here.
It has a natural asphalt lake that is dug up to pave roads.

capital-pan.summary: A country on the narrow isthmus that links the two American continents. Its capital shares the country's name.
facts: The Panama Canal links the Pacific and the Atlantic.
Control of the canal passed from the United States to Panama in 1999.

capital-pry.summary: A landlocked South American country whose flag has different designs on the front and back. The capital is Asunción.
facts: Spanish and Guaraní are both official languages.
It runs the Itaipu Dam jointly with Brazil.

capital-per.summary: An Andean country known for ceviche, a raw-fish dish, and alpacas. The capital is Lima.
facts: Machu Picchu is a mountaintop city built by the Inca Empire.
Giant geoglyphs are etched into the Nazca plains.

capital-flk.summary: A British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic, off the southern tip of South America. The capital is Stanley.
facts: In 1982 the United Kingdom and Argentina went to war over these islands.
Sheep and penguins far outnumber people.

capital-pri.summary: A self-governing U.S. territory at the eastern end of the Greater Antilles. The capital is San Juan.
facts: Residents are U.S. citizens but cannot vote in the presidential general election.
El Yunque is the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. National Forest System.

capital-guf.summary: An overseas department of France in northeastern South America. The capital is Cayenne.
facts: Europe's space rockets launch from Kourou.
Devil's Island, the penal colony where Dreyfus was imprisoned, lies offshore.

capital-gum.summary: A U.S. island at the southern end of the Mariana Islands. The capital is Hagåtña.
facts: It is nicknamed “Where America's Day Begins.”
The language and culture of the Indigenous Chamorro people live on here.

capital-nru.summary: A coral island nation in the Pacific just south of the equator. The de facto capital is Yaren.
facts: At 21 square kilometers, it is the third-smallest country in the world, after Vatican City and Monaco.
It once grew very rich mining and selling phosphate formed from hardened bird droppings.

capital-nfk.summary: An Australian island in the Pacific whose flag shows the pine tree named after it. The capital is Kingston.
facts: It was a British penal colony.
Descendants of the Bounty mutineers moved here and still live on the island.

capital-ncl.summary: A French overseas territory in Melanesia in the South Pacific, ringed by a World Heritage–listed lagoon. The capital is Nouméa.
facts: Rich in nickel, it is one of the world's leading producers.
It has held several referendums on whether to remain part of France.

capital-nzl.summary: A South Pacific nation made up of two main islands. The capital is Wellington.
facts: In 1893 it became the first country in the world where women voted in parliamentary elections.
Before matches, the All Blacks rugby team performs the haka, a Māori dance.

capital-niu.summary: A remote South Pacific island that has issued Pokémon coins as legal tender. The capital is Alofi.
facts: It is a single rock island formed by uplifted coral.
It governs itself in free association with New Zealand.

capital-mhl.summary: A coral island nation north of the equator whose land is at risk of disappearing under rising seas. The capital is Majuro.
facts: The bikini swimsuit is named after Bikini Atoll, where the U.S. carried out nuclear tests.
Traditional navigation charts made of sticks lashed together to map ocean swells have been handed down.

capital-fsm.summary: A western Pacific island federation that includes Yap, known for its giant stone money. The capital is Palikir.
facts: It is a federation of four states with more than 600 islands.
The ruins of Nan Madol are built from stacked stone columns on the sea.

capital-vut.summary: A volcanic South Pacific island nation with an underwater post office where you can mail waterproof postcards. The capital is Port Vila.
facts: The active volcano Mount Yasur is constantly belching smoke.
It has a traditional ritual that inspired bungee jumping.

capital-mnp.summary: U.S. islands in the western Pacific with resorts popular among honeymooners. The capital is Saipan.
facts: It includes the island where the Battle of Saipan was fought in World War II.
As a self-governing U.S. territory, its residents hold U.S. citizenship.

capital-wsm.summary: A South Pacific island nation where “Treasure Island” author Robert Louis Stevenson spent his last years and is buried. The capital is Apia.
facts: In 2011 it moved to the west side of the International Date Line, skipping December 30 entirely.
The English word “tattoo” comes from “tatau,” a Polynesian word used here, in Tahiti and elsewhere.

capital-slb.summary: A South Pacific island nation where traditional money made of strung shells is still in use. The capital is Honiara.
facts: It includes the island where the Battle of Guadalcanal was fought in World War II.
It is made up of six large islands and more than 900 smaller ones.

capital-asm.summary: A U.S. territory in South Pacific Polynesia, home to the only U.S. national park south of the equator. The capital is Pago Pago.
facts: Lying east of the International Date Line, it is a day behind neighboring Samoa.
It produces an unusually large number of American football players for a U.S. territory.

capital-wlf.summary: Remote French islands at the western edge of Polynesia in the South Pacific. The capital is Mata-Utu.
facts: Although it is French territory, it still has three traditional kings.
Isolated in the South Pacific, it is served by few boats.

capital-cck.summary: Australian islands in the eastern Indian Ocean made up of two coral atolls. The capital is West Island.
facts: Charles Darwin studied how coral islands form here.
It is Australian territory, but most residents are of Malay descent.

capital-cok.summary: Islands in the heart of South Pacific Polynesia that include Aitutaki Lagoon. The capital is Avarua.
facts: It consists of 15 islands, and residents also hold New Zealand citizenship.
It is named after the explorer James Cook.

capital-cxr.summary: An Australian island in the Indian Ocean south of Java. The capital is Flying Fish Cove.
facts: Every year tens of millions of red crabs march to the sea.
It got its name because it was discovered on Christmas Day.

capital-kir.summary: A nation of coral islands scattered along the equator in the Pacific. The capital is South Tarawa.
facts: Thanks to the International Date Line, it is the first place on Earth to welcome the New Year.
Both the equator and the 180th meridian pass through it, so it spans all four hemispheres.

capital-tkl.summary: Three New Zealand atolls in South Pacific Polynesia. There is no official capital.
facts: With no airport, it can only be reached by a boat trip of more than a day from Samoa.
Almost all of its electricity comes from solar power.

capital-ton.summary: A South Pacific island kingdom whose constitution bans doing business on Sundays. The capital is Nuku'alofa.
facts: It was a British protectorate for 70 years from 1900 but never gave up its sovereignty.
Only 45 of its 171 islands are inhabited.

capital-tuv.summary: The world's fourth-smallest country, made up of nine low-lying coral islands in the South Pacific. The capital is Funafuti.
facts: Its highest point is less than 5 meters above sea level, leaving it vulnerable to rising seas.
Leasing out its .tv internet domain is a major source of income.

capital-png.summary: A country covering the eastern half of a large South Pacific island, with its national bird, the bird-of-paradise, on its flag. The capital is Port Moresby.
facts: With around 840 languages spoken, it has more languages than any other country.
The western half of the island belongs to Indonesia, so a straight border cuts across the island from north to south.

capital-plw.summary: A small western Pacific island nation that declared the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009. The capital is Ngerulmud.
facts: In 2006 the capital moved from Koror to Ngerulmud.
Scuba diving is banned at Jellyfish Lake, so visitors can only snorkel.

capital-pyf.summary: A French overseas territory of 118 South Pacific islands, where the first overwater bungalows were built in 1967. The capital is Papeete.
facts: It includes Tahiti, where Paul Gauguin went to paint.
Tahitian black pearls are its signature export.

capital-fji.summary: A South Pacific island nation whose name is familiar from a bottled-water brand. The capital is Suva.
facts: It is made up of more than 300 islands.
Its gold medal in rugby sevens in 2016 was the country's first-ever Olympic medal.

capital-pcn.summary: A remote British Overseas Territory in the middle of the South Pacific. The capital is Adamstown.
facts: The Bounty mutineers hid on this island and settled there.
It is often cited as the least populous inhabited territory in the world.

capital-aus.summary: Home to kangaroos and koalas, a country that takes up an entire continent. The capital is Canberra.
facts: When Sydney and Melbourne competed to be the capital, Canberra was built from scratch as a compromise.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world.
